Rashi on Ketubot 67b:12:1.english: The socket of the door - A hole in the threshold in which the pivot of the door turns.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:12:2.english: That day - That [same] day on which the pauper set his mind to know who was giving them to him.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:13:1.english: When he saw - the poor man.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:13:2.hebrew: אנא שכיחנא בגו ביתא - ועניים מוצאין אותי, לפיכך זכותי גדול:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:13:2.english: I am found inside the house - And poor people find me; therefore, my merit is great.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:13:3.hebrew: ומקרבא הנייתי - הנאתי מזומנת, שאני מחלקת לחם ובשר ומלח, אבל אתה נותן מעות לעניים והם טורחים וקונים סעודה:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:13:3.english: And my benefit is near - My benefit is ready [at hand], for I distribute bread, meat, and salt, whereas you give money to the poor, and they [must] exert themselves and buy a meal.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:14:1.english: What [is] all this - Why [did] they [need] to flee and enter the oven?

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:14:2.hebrew: היא מוצאת - והיא שלחה וגו'. אע"פ שבאתה לישרף, לא גילתה הדבר אלא אם כן יגלה הוא, ואם לא יגלה — נשרפת:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:14:2.english: She was brought forth - "And she sent," etc. Even though she came to be burned, she did not reveal the matter unless he would reveal [it]; and if he would not reveal [it], she would be burned.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:15:1.english: He doubled them - He doubled them.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:16:2.english: My provisions are light - I have prepared light provisions for a long journey upon which I am setting out.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:17:1.hebrew: ומצלי עיניה - ומטה עיניו כלפי אחוריו לראות שלא יבא רמאי ויתירה, שעושה עצמו עני; והעניים באים ומתירים אותם:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:17:1.english: And he would incline his eyes - And he turns his eyes behind him to see that a swindler does not come and untie it, [one] who makes himself [out to be] poor, while the poor come and untie them.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:1:1.hebrew: שבאו לינשא - משל צדקה, דאמרינן לקמן: "אשר יחסר לו", זו אשה:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:1:1.english: Who have come to be married - From [the] charity [fund], as we say later: "which he lacks" — this [refers to] a wife.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:4:1.english: Of poultry - For their price is high, and he was delicate.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:4:2.hebrew: בליטרא בשר - שהיה בשר ביוקר, והיה צריך בשר בדמי ליטרא מעות:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:4:2.english: For a litra, meat - For meat was expensive, and he needed meat [costing] the value of a litra of coins.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:4:3.english: It was a small village - and the remainder was not sold.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:4:4.hebrew: אמטולתיה - בשבילו, והיינו רבותא. ולעולם במשקל ליטרא בשר קאמר:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:4:4.english: For him - [Meaning] for his sake, and that is the novelty [of the incident]. And actually, [Rav Ashi] is speaking of a litra weight of meat.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:5:1.english: A certain [person] who came - A poor man seeking sustenance.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:5:2.english: On what do you dine - What are you accustomed to eating at your meal?

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:6:1.hebrew: בעתו - הכל לפי מה שהוא צריך, כל יחיד ויחיד לפי לימודו:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:6:1.english: In its time - Everything according to what he needs, each and every individual according to what he is accustomed to.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:7:1.hebrew: אמר רבא מאי דקמא - מה דבר זה שאירע לפני עתה, שלא הייתי רגיל בכך, שבאת זו לכאן ותרנגולת ויין ישן בידה:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:7:1.english: Rava said: What is [this] that [is] before [me] - What is this thing that happened before me now, that I was not accustomed to this, that this [woman] came here with a hen and aged wine in her hand?

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:7:2.english: I have responded to you - I spoke too much.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:8:1.english: He does not have - [anything] of his own.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:8:2.english: And does not want to be supported - From charity [funds].

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:9:1.hebrew: יש לו ואינו רוצה להתפרנס - משלו, אלא משל צדקה, ומסגף עצמו ברעב:
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:9:1.english: He has [means] and does not want to support himself - from his own [funds], rather from charity, and afflicts himself with hunger.

Rashi on Ketubot 67b:9:2.hebrew: שתזוח דעתו עליו - יגבה לבו לומר: "דעתם לחזור ולגבות הימני, הואיל ותבעוני משכון, אין זו אלא הלואה", ויטול בלא בושת, שיאמר: "אין לי משכון", והם יאמרו: "טול בלא משכון":
Rashi on Ketubot 67b:9:2.english: So that his mindset should be raised for him - His heart will be lifted up to say, "Their intention is to come back and collect from me; since they demanded collateral from me, this is nothing other than a loan," and he will take [it] without shame, for he will say, "I have no collateral," and they will say, "Take [it] without collateral."

Tosafot on Ketubot 67b:11:1.hebrew: וחכ"א יש לו ואינו רוצה להתפרנס אין נזקקין לו - הני חכמים הם ר"ש דלעיל. וא"ת: והא לית ליה לר' שמעון "דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם" במסכת ראש השנה (דף ח.), ועוד, הא דדרשינן בפרק אלו מציאות (ב"מ דף לא:): "הקם תקים", "השב תשיב" — אפי' מאה פעמים, אטו כולהו דלא כר"ש? ואומר ר"י, דכל היכא דאיכא למידרש — דרשינן, ולא אמרינן "דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם"; אלא הכא, דלא מסתבר ליה למדרש כרבנן, דקרא משמע דבאין לו מיירי, כדכתיב: "די מחסורו":
Tosafot on Ketubot 67b:11:1.english: And the Sages say: [If] he has [means] and does not want to support himself, they do not get involved with him - These Sages are Rabbi Shimon [mentioned] above. And if you ask: Does Rabbi Shimon not hold [the principle that] "the Torah spoke in the language of men" in Tractate Rosh Hashanah (8a)? And furthermore, [regarding] that which we expound in the chapter [entitled] Elu Metzi'ot (Bava Metzia 31b): "You shall surely raise" [and] "You shall surely return" — [meaning] even a hundred times — are all of those not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon? And the Ri says that wherever there is [a way] to expound, we expound [it] and do not say "the Torah spoke in the language of men"; except here, where it does not seem reasonable to him to expound like the Rabbis, because the verse implies that it is speaking of one who does not have [means], as it is written: "sufficient for his need."

Tosafot on Ketubot 67b:11:2.hebrew: וחכ"א יש לו ואינו רוצה להתפרנס אין נזקקין לו - הני חכמים הם ר"ש דלעיל. וא"ת: והא לית ליה לר' שמעון "דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם" במסכת ראש השנה (דף ח.); ועוד, הא דדרשינן בפרק אלו מציאות (ב"מ דף לא:) "הקם תקים", "השב תשיב" — אפי' מאה פעמים, אטו כולהו דלא כר"ש? ואומר ר"י: דכל היכא דאיכא למידרש — דרשינן, ולא אמרינן "דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם", אלא הכא, דלא מסתבר ליה למדרש כרבנן, דקרא משמע דבאין לו מיירי, כדכתיב: "די מחסורו":
Tosafot on Ketubot 67b:11:2.english: And the Sages say: [If] he has [money] and does not want to support [himself], they do not get involved with him - These Sages are R. Shimon [mentioned] above. And if you ask: But R. Shimon does not hold [the principle that] "the Torah spoke in the language of men" in tractate Rosh Hashanah (8a); and furthermore, that which we expound in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Metziot (Bava Metzia 31b): "You shall surely raise [it]" [and] "You shall surely return [it]" — even a hundred times, is it [possible that] all of them are not in accordance with R. Shimon? And R. Yitzchak says: Wherever there is [something] to expound, we expound [it] and do not say "the Torah spoke in the language of men," except here, where it does not seem reasonable to him to expound [it] like the Rabbis, because the verse implies that it is speaking of one who does not have [money], as it is written: "sufficient for his need."

Tosafot on Ketubot 67b:14:1.hebrew: דכתיב היא מוצאת - רבינו חננאל גריס מוצת בלא אל"ף, לשון "ויצת אש בציון" (איכה ד׳:י״א):
Tosafot on Ketubot 67b:14:1.english: As it is written: "She was brought forth" - Rabbeinu Chananel reads [the word as] mutzet without an alef, [from the same] expression [as] "and He kindled [vayatzet] a fire in Zion" (Lamentations 4:11).
